name: Baba Zakura
age_estimate: roughly 1,000 years (traditional/legendary figure repeated by the village and prefecture, not a growth-rate dating)

location.address: Ishibashi, Tamai, Otama Village, Adachi District, Fukushima Prefecture (within the grounds of Fukumitsu Kokuzo-do temple)

access: Free. Stands within the grounds of Fukumitsu Kokuzo-do temple, Otama Village; temple grounds are open. 15 min by car from Motomiya IC (Tohoku Expwy) or 10 min by car from Motomiya Station.
transport: Motomiya Station (JR Tohoku Main Line), about 10 minutes by car; no direct public transit noted to the site itself.
verify_notes: National Natural Monument since 16 Dec 1936, also a Fukushima Prefectural 'Green Cultural Property' since 1983. Edo-higan cherry, legend says it grew from a cherry-wood whip Minamoto no Yoshiie stuck in the ground to tether horses during the Later Three Years' War (late Heian period); the site was the cavalry training ground (baba) for his troops, hence the name. Also called the 'seed-sowing cherry' because its bloom (~late April) traditionally signalled when to sow rice. 1936 survey recorded it at ~21m tall, trunk girth 7.45m at 1.5m height, root girth 11.1m; current village page gives a shorter 15m height, 7m trunk girth, 10m root girth, reflecting damage since then. FLAG: on 1 March 2018 the tree toppled at its base in strong winds; the upper trunk was cut back and it was hauled upright again by local residents and a preservation society. Japanese sources (village site, ja.Wikipedia, arukikata.co.jp) describe it as still in serious decline with active vitality-recovery work ongoing ('衰弱が著しく樹勢回復作業が懸命に行われている'), blooming only sparsely from remaining young branches each April. A Wikimedia Commons photo dated 25 Oct 2023, geotagged to this exact spot (37°31'51.63"N 140°21'54.08"E, matching the given coordinates precisely), shows the tree still standing, which is the freshest alive-evidence found. This is a damaged, actively-recovering veteran, not a fully healthy specimen: worth including but the story and access line should be honest that it fell in 2018 and is recovering rather than presenting it as pristine. Two independent sources (village official page, ja.Wikipedia) agree on species, age tradition and designation; a third (arukikata.co.jp) corroborates the 2018 fall and recovery narrative in more detail.
